name: Jefferson Deadlift
instructions: Straddle the bar with one foot forward and one foot back, feet offset like a staggered stance.
Grip the bar with one hand in front of your body and one hand behind it.
Stand up by driving through both legs and extending your hips, keeping the bar close to your straddled stance.
Lower under control and switch stance halfway through your sets to balance the asymmetry.

name: Safety Bar Squat
instructions: Rack a safety squat bar so the padded yoke sits across your shoulders and the handles fall forward.
Unrack and step back, holding the handles for stability rather than pulling down on them.
Squat down until your hip crease passes below your knee, then drive back up.
Expect more forward lean than a straight bar squat; keep your chest tall against it.

name: Anderson Squat
instructions: Set safety pins or blocks in a rack at your bottom squat depth.
Start each rep from a dead stop on the pins with no stretch reflex, then squat up.
Reset fully between reps rather than lowering back to the pins under control.
Unlike the Zercher squat, the bar rests across your back or front rack, not in your elbow creases.

name: Pause Squat
instructions: Perform a normal back or front squat descent.
Hold the bottom position for two to five seconds without relaxing or bouncing.
Drive up out of the pause with the same bar path and bracing as the descent.
Use a lighter load than your regular squat until the pause feels stable.

name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
instructions: Take a wide, snatch-width overhand grip on the bar, well outside your shoulders.
Set your hips lower than a conventional deadlift to reach the bar at this width.
Drive through the floor and extend your hips and knees together to stand up.
Expect a longer range of motion and more upper-back demand than a conventional pull.

name: Shrimp Squat
instructions: Stand on one leg and hold the other foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Bend the standing knee and lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor.
Push back up through the standing leg without using the trailing leg for help.
Hold a wall or rail for balance while learning the pattern.

name: Archer Pull-Up
instructions: Start from a wide-grip pull-up bar hang.
Pull up and shift your weight toward one hand, straightening the opposite arm out to the side.
Bring your chin near the bent-arm hand, then lower back to a dead hang.
Alternate sides, or work one side fully before switching.

name: Wall Walk
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your feet against a wall.
Walk your feet up the wall while walking your hands back toward it, keeping your body straight.
Stop when your chest nears the wall in a near-handstand position.
Reverse the walk back down to the floor to complete one rep.

name: Dragon Flag
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip behind your head for anchor.
Raise your legs and hips off the bench until only your upper back stays in contact.
Lower your body as one straight rigid line, stopping just before your hips touch down.
Raise back to the top without letting your lower back sag.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel on a pad and hold the wheel with both hands beneath your shoulders.
Roll the wheel forward, extending your body while keeping your core braced.
Stop before your lower back arches, then pull back to the start using your abs.
Shorten the range of motion until full rollouts stay pain-free.

name: Skin The Cat
instructions: Hang from rings or a bar with an overhand grip.
Tuck your knees and roll your hips through your arms until you invert behind them.
Continue until your feet point toward the floor behind you.
Reverse the motion back to a normal hang, controlling the descent throughout.

name: Ring Row
instructions: Set gymnastic rings at waist to chest height and grip one in each hand.
Lean back with arms extended and feet on the floor, body in a straight line.
Pull your chest toward the rings, keeping elbows close to your sides.
Lower with control; walk your feet closer to the anchor to increase difficulty.

name: Broad Jump
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart at a marked start line.
Swing your arms back and bend your knees, then jump forward as far as possible.
Land softly on both feet with your knees bent to absorb the impact.
Measure from the start line to your rearmost heel on landing.

name: Man Maker
instructions: Start in a push-up position holding a pair of dumbbells.
Perform a push-up, then row each dumbbell to your hip one side at a time.
Jump your feet to your hands and stand up, curling the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Press the dumbbells overhead, then return to the push-up position to repeat.

name: Devil Press
instructions: Start standing with a dumbbell in each hand.
Drop into a burpee, planking with the dumbbells on the floor beneath your shoulders.
Explode your feet back in and swing the dumbbells up into an overhead snatch as you stand.
Reset your stance and repeat immediately for the next rep.

name: GHD Sit-Up
instructions: Lock your ankles under the pads of a glute-ham developer with hips on the pad.
Lower your torso back past parallel until you feel a stretch through your abs.
Curl back up to a fully upright finish, using your abs rather than momentum.
Limit the range of motion at first; the extended stretch loads the spine hard.

name: Copenhagen Plank
instructions: Lie on your side and prop your top foot on a bench, with your bottom leg free beneath it.
Support your upper body on your forearm, forming a straight line from shoulder to top foot.
Hold the position, keeping hips level and lifted off the floor.
Start with the bottom knee bent for support, extending it fully as the hold gets stronger.

name: Pendlay Row
instructions: Set up over a bar on the floor with a flat back and torso close to parallel with the ground.
Grip the bar and pull it explosively into your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Let the bar return to a full dead stop on the floor after each rep.
Reset your position fully between reps rather than bouncing the plates.

name: Jefferson Curl
instructions: Stand on a raised platform holding a light barbell or dumbbell against your thighs.
Starting from the neck, round your spine downward one vertebra at a time.
Let the weight pull you into a deep forward fold once your spine is fully rounded.
Reverse the curl from the tailbone up, stacking your spine back to standing.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored firmly, either by a partner or a fixed pad.
Keeping your hips extended, lower your torso toward the floor as slowly as possible.
Use your hamstrings to resist the fall for as long as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands and push back up, or return to kneeling if strong enough.

name: Poliquin Step-Up
instructions: Stand facing a step or box roughly knee height, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Place your whole foot on the box without pushing off your trailing leg.
Drive through the lead leg only to stand fully on the box.
Step back down under control and repeat all reps on one side before switching.

name: Peterson Step-Up
instructions: Stand facing a low step with your lead foot planted and torso leaning slightly forward.
Drive up through the lead leg while keeping the trailing leg relaxed and light.
Pause briefly at the top with the hip extended before lowering back down.
Keep the movement slow to emphasize knee control through the full range.

name: ATG Split Squat
instructions: Set up in a deep split stance with your rear foot elevated behind you.
Lower straight down until your rear knee nearly touches the floor and your front shin travels well past your toes.
Drive back up through the front leg to standing.
Work within a range your ankle and knee tolerate, and progress the depth gradually.

name: KOT Split Squat
instructions: Set up in a split stance with your rear foot elevated behind you on a bench or box.
Descend while deliberately letting your front knee travel forward over your toes.
Keep your heel planted and control the knee's forward path rather than avoiding it.
Drive back up through the front leg, then reset before the next rep.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand a couple of feet in front of a bench and rest the top of your rear foot on it.
Lower straight down until your front thigh is close to parallel, keeping your torso upright.
Drive back up through the front leg to standing.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand for load, or do it bodyweight-only while learning the balance.

name: Running
instructions: Run at the prescribed pace for the prescribed time or distance.

name: Walking
instructions: Walk at a brisk pace for the prescribed time or distance.

name: Otago Hip Abduction
instructions: Stand tall holding a chair back, lift one leg sideways keeping knee straight and toes forward.
Lower with control, repeat, then switch legs.

name: Otago Toe Raise
instructions: Stand with feet flat, lift toes and forefoot off the floor keeping heels down.
Lower with control and repeat.

name: Otago Tandem Stance
instructions: Stand with one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe, and hold.
Use a chair or wall for support at lower levels.

name: Otago Heel Toe Walk
instructions: Walk forward placing the heel of one foot directly against the toes of the other with each step.
Keep gaze forward, arms free for balance.

name: Otago One Leg Stand
instructions: Stand on one leg, holding a chair or wall at lower levels for support.
Hold, then switch legs; progress by removing support.

name: Otago Backwards Walking
instructions: Walk backward in a straight line for the prescribed number of steps, keeping a clear path behind you.
Progress by removing support or adding head turns.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Two-hand hip hinge swing to chest height; hips drive, arms stay loose.

name: Pistol Squat
instructions: Single-leg squat to full depth with the free leg held forward; stand back up without touching down.

name: Negative Pull-Up
instructions: Jump or step to the top of a pull-up and lower under control over 3-5 seconds.

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Push-up with hands close, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond under the chest.
